Both ship together; the listener picks at runtime per the spec. Native path includes the per-connection driver, the listener with O(1) demux + random SCID, and per-stream backpressure retention. PostgreSQL wire reintroduction discovery: upstream pgwire 0.28 server-api is tokio-coupled and allocation-heavy; Proxima needs a sans-IO codec crate plus a prime/proxima stream facade instead of embedding pgwire. TLS is existing capability via proxima-tls, not new pgwire-owned protocol work. The target is full PostgreSQL wire capability; phases are sequencing, not scope reduction.

PostgreSQL wire support: proxima-protocols::pgwire_codec (sans-IO no_std no-alloc message codec + session FSM, full protocol matrix incl. messages upstream pgwire omits, folded from the former proxima-pgwire-codec crate) + proxima-pgwire facade: futures-io driver, two mounts (PgWireAnyProtocol for the universal listener's classifier, PgWireListenProtocol standalone), TLS via SSLRequest or a PostgreSQL 17 direct-TLS ClientHello, trust/cleartext/MD5/SCRAM auth, COPY in+out, LISTEN/NOTIFY, portal suspension, cooperative cancel, plus a client half (sans-IO ClientSession, blocking PgClient, PgwireClientUpstream pipe). The SQL engine is a QueryRequest -> PgReply pipe; there is no handler trait. Proof mechanism is scripts/proxima-pgwire-gate.sh + .github/workflows/proxima-pgwire.yml (real-PostgreSQL differential included); there is no discipline log.

ResilientSink (telemetry::out::resilient) buffers ahead of any OTLP transport so the shared drain never blocks on a slow/unreachable collector: forever-retrying capped backoff, reconnect-on-error, per-severity retention-horizon shedding (defaults 10/20/30/35/40 min trace-error, validated monotonic ladder), survivable-seconds gauges, aggregated drop announcements. Guarantees liveness, not losslessness.

Hot-path requirements and source rules: 500MB RAM cap, >=55MB/s, <1ms p99, zero-copy and no heap allocation on query/scoring/inner-loop paths, lock-free reads, lock discipline (lock-free > async gate > proxima_lock::Mutex, never a bare mutex, never a spin), no O(n^2), box-free by default, RPITIT for trait-async. Prose rules, hand-curated. AGENTS.md is the single source of truth; this record exists only so ai_docs relations can point at it.

ExpertSlab can retain a selected high-precision expert as Arc<Mmap> plus byte range and emits the same per-step ExpertSource without copying the whole expert set. Its memory report keeps heap-owned payload bytes separate from mapped address-space ranges; mapped_bytes is intentionally not an RSS claim.

One DynaExq address is a transformer-layer/expert pair, while the gathered runtime has three independently bound gate/up/down projection sites. ExpertSlab records an O(1) model-layer/projection-to-site table at bind time; a HOBBIT promotion or eviction must change all three sites before the gather snapshot.

Vulkan WGPU embedding exposed a broadcast-reduce output-coverage defect: RMSNorm-shaped folds have logical output [1,1024] but output_axes [0] plus epilogue_broadcast_axes [1]. The WGPU cooperative renderer must use full-rank coordinates, full output extents, and contiguous output strides; after that correction the vector is no longer one-hot but layer-0 parity remains RED.

Default-off qwen35moe-linked-suffix uses partition_between_with_mapping to expand only the final gather through the logits root, then excludes already-returned outputs from standalone suffix evaluation. Every router/residency boundary and current-layer expert binding stays on its existing path. Earlier-layer linking was not selected because dense-attention and SSM placements currently use current-layer ownership. Synthetic tests compare router, gather, and logits bits plus extra original-id cuts; real-model GPU output and performance remain unmeasured for this feature.

SPICE (arXiv:2608.21240) and SpecMD (arXiv:2602.03921) map to an advisory DynaExq prefetch pipe: confidence-aware lookahead may warm low/high ExpertSource entries, but the actual router remains authoritative and misses fall back to exact low-codec sources. Track hit rate, overfetch bytes, page-in wait, TTFT, and TTNT separately.

APEX (arXiv:2608.11688) and MoE-APEX provide confidence-aware pre-attention and layer-level expert prefetch; Beyond Routing (arXiv:2608.08853) keeps selected IDs and router mass fixed while changing post-dispatch aggregation commitment. APEX maps to an advisory DynaExq predictor; Beyond Routing is a separate algebra seam and must not alter residency admission or authoritative routing.

ExpertResidency::prefetch_candidates emits fixed-capacity, confidence-filtered, de-duplicated warming candidates without mutating EMA, residency, or authoritative routing. It is the APEX/SPICE predictor seam; page and evict remain explicit step-boundary actions.

Cloud-Grade Local MoE Inference (arXiv:2606.10493), CoX-MoE (arXiv:2605.17889), Speculating Experts (arXiv:2603.19289), pre-attention expert prediction (arXiv:2511.10676), Multi-Layer Scheduling (arXiv:2602.21626), and NANOZK (arXiv:2603.18046) map respectively to phase-separated prefill/decode scheduling, route-compatible coalescing, advisory predictor positions, three-level scheduling, and an inspectable layer proof boundary. summary: Universal Client TLS root settings must survive ClientBuilder/config specs, canonical HTTP forwarding, and the prime HTTP or gRPC TLS constructors. Universal Listener mTLS custom CA bundle paths are carried by its TLS terminator config. Client defaults use native verification on Windows; listener mTLS uses explicit client-CA anchors. Hyper owns ALPN negotiation, so the rustls ALPN vector must be empty when handed to HttpsConnectorBuilder.
abandoned_designs: Configuring TlsStreamUpstream directly without forwarding the policy through the universal Client leaves real HTTPS requests on hard-coded Mozilla roots.
Applying outbound OS trust roots implicitly to an inbound listener would change mTLS policy without operator selection.
Passing the client's default ALPN list unchanged to hyper-rustls conflicts with connector-owned HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 negotiation.
Keeping AliasFactory unix-only while registering it on both unix and Windows leaves the Windows both-wires build without its factory type.
evidence_status: host TLS and facade tests passed; Windows proxima, proxima-http Hyper, and http-hyper alias cross-target checks passed; see AC11/AC12 evidence
